optional_codes.reason: The note states that the patient's mother had glaucoma. The guidelines allow a family history code on any record and do not require it. Either answer is defensible.

citations.case: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines FY2027, Section I.C.7.a.1 (assign as many glaucoma codes as needed to identify the type of glaucoma, the affected eye and the glaucoma stage); Section I.B.13 (laterality: the code names the side documented); Section IV.J (history codes may be used as secondary codes if the family history has an impact on current care or influences treatment); Section I.C.21.c.4 (history codes are acceptable on any medical record regardless of the reason for visit); Section IV.G (list first the diagnosis chiefly responsible for the services provided)

coder_notes: Primary open-angle glaucoma is documented in the right eye at moderate stage; the 7th character carries the stage. The left eye has no glaucoma, so the bilateral code (H40.1132) is not used. The raised pressure, the disc findings and the visual field defect are attributed to the glaucoma and are not coded separately. Family history of glaucoma is accepted but not required (see optional_codes). Traps: a 7th character for mild, severe, indeterminate or unspecified stage; the bilateral code because both eyes are examined; an ocular hypertension code from the raised pressure; a glaucoma suspect code
